findings.title: NATS health check publishes to unconfirmed stream
findings.explanation: monitor.js assumes any publish success means NATS is healthy, but natsController.js does NOT await the server ACK (js.publish returns void). A publish can appear to succeed while the message is lost or the connection is already broken, causing false 'ok' status.
findings.fix: Use the JetStream publish response or add a subscriber that echoes back to confirm end-to-end delivery before marking 'ok'.

findings.title: Redis connection promise races and can resolve before ready
findings.explanation: If the client emits 'error' before 'ready', the promise rejects and connect() throws, but the Redis object is still created and may auto-reconnect. Subsequent calls to connect() skip creation (status === 'ready' never becomes true) yet operations fail silently because the original client is in an error state.
findings.fix: Recreate the client on each connect attempt or verify client.status === 'ready' inside the promise.

findings.title: modelComms re-uses single callback for both direct and broadcast messages
findings.explanation: Gemini assigned the same directMessageHandler to NATS subscriptions for 'direct.${modelId}' and 'broadcast.all'. A model receiving its own broadcastEcho will invoke the handler twice (once as broadcast, once as direct if payload matches), causing duplicate processing and potential feedback loops.
findings.fix: Use separate handler variables or filter by msg.to/msg.channel inside the handler.

findings.title: generateId can collide within same millisecond
findings.explanation: Two calls in the same millisecond produce the same timestamp prefix; Math.random() collision probability is low but non-zero, leading to duplicate message IDs and history overwrites in Redis.
findings.fix: Include a per-process counter or use uuid/v4.

findings.title: monitor never emits modelOnline events
findings.code: // Emit events for models that went offline
findings.explanation: computeModelStats only emits 'modelOffline'. Components expecting symmetrical 'modelOnline' events will never receive them, breaking any auto-retry or discovery logic that relies on that event.
findings.fix: Compare oldList vs newList and emit 'modelOnline' for ids that appear in newList but not oldList.

findings.title: Redis connection not established before use in setMessage
findings.explanation: The setMessage function assumes redisClient is already connected and ready. However, there is no guarantee that connect() has been called before setMessage is invoked. If redisClient is undefined or not connected, this will throw an error.
findings.fix: Call await connect() at the start of setMessage (and other functions like getMessage, setModelState, etc.) if redisClient is not ready.

findings.title: NATS subscription in modelComms uses same durable name across multiple instances
findings.explanation: The durable consumer name `consumer-${modelId}` is the same for each model. However, if multiple instances of the same modelId subscribe (e.g., after a restart), they will conflict because NATS JetStream durable consumers must be unique per subscription group. The code in natsController.js uses opts.durable(consumerGroup) and opts.deliverTo(createInbox()) which creates a queue subscription. If two instances use same durable name, they will compete for messages, but the deliverTo creates a unique inbox, causing mismatch and potential message loss.
findings.fix: Either make the durable name unique per instance (e.g., include a random suffix) or ensure only one subscriber per modelId exists.

findings.title: Heartbeat overwrites existing state in modelComms
findings.explanation: The heartbeat interval merges existing state with new fields, but existing may be null or a string (if setModelState was called with a string). If existing is a string, spreading it with ...existing will cause an error because strings are not spreadable objects. Also, the setModelState in redisController.js stores data as JSON string, but getModelState returns parsed object or string. If existing is a string, the spread will break.
findings.fix: Ensure existing is an object before spreading. For example: const state = typeof existing === 'object' ? existing : {}; await redis.setModelState(modelId, { ...state, status: 'online', lastHeartbeat: Date.now() });

findings.title: Monitor's checkNatsHealth publishes to a subject that may not have a stream
findings.explanation: The nats.publish function in natsController.js uses js.publish which requires the subject to be associated with a stream if JetStream is enabled. The stream subjects defined in natsController.js are 'direct.>', 'broadcast.>', 'channel.>'. 'health.ping' does not match any stream, so the publish will fail with 'no stream matches subject' error, causing health check to always report 'down'.
findings.fix: Either add a stream for health subjects, or use core NATS publish (nc.publish) instead of JetStream. Alternatively, change the subject to match an existing stream pattern, e.g., 'broadcast.health'.

findings.title: Redis setMessage uses messageId.split(':')[0] for channel, which may be incorrect
findings.explanation: The channel extraction assumes messageId format like 'direct:abc' or 'broadcast:def'. However, if messageId does not contain ':', split returns the whole string, causing channel to be the full messageId. This may lead to many history streams (e.g., history:direct:abc) instead of aggregated per channel. Not critical but suboptimal.
findings.fix: Use a more robust method to extract channel, perhaps pass channel as a parameter to setMessage.

findings.title: NATS subscribe in modelComms does not handle subscription errors
findings.explanation: The subscribe call is awaited, but if it fails (e.g., due to network issue), the error is not caught. This could cause init to fail silently because the async function is not wrapped in try-catch. However, the nats.subscribe function itself may throw, but the init function does not have error handling for that line.
findings.fix: Wrap the subscription in a try-catch and log or handle the error appropriately.

findings.title: Redis getAllModels may return null if no models, causing iteration error
findings.explanation: If there are no models in the hash, redisClient.hgetall returns null (or empty object? ioredis returns empty object). The documentation says hgetall returns an object of key-values; if hash doesn't exist, returns empty object. However, if it returns null, Object.entries(null) throws. Need to verify behavior. Assuming it returns empty object, it's fine. But if it returns null, it's critical.
findings.fix: Check if states is null or undefined before iterating: states = states || {};

findings.title: Test uses nats.subscribe with durable consumer that may conflict across test runs
findings.explanation: The test uses a durable consumer name that includes testRunId to avoid conflicts. However, if the test fails and does not clean up, the durable consumer will remain in NATS JetStream, potentially causing issues in subsequent test runs. Not critical but could cause test flakiness.
findings.fix: Ensure test cleanup deletes the consumer or use ephemeral consumers (no durable).

findings.title: broadcast.all subject mismatch between modelComms and natsController
findings.explanation: modelComms.js calls nats.broadcast() with the entire message object, but natsController.js's broadcast() function expects a plain payload (not a message object) and wraps it in JSON. This causes a TypeError when JSON.stringify tries to serialize the message because it already contains a stringified payload.
findings.fix: Change modelComms.js line 39 to: await nats.broadcast(msg.payload);

findings.title: NATS stream subject mismatch for CITY_BROADCAST
findings.explanation: The CITY_BROADCAST stream is created with subject 'broadcast.>', but modelComms.js publishes broadcasts to 'broadcast.all' (via nats.broadcast()). The 'broadcast.all' subject does not match 'broadcast.>' pattern, so messages are not persisted in the CITY_BROADCAST stream, causing data loss and breaking message history.
findings.fix: Change line 34 in natsController.js to: 'broadcast.*' or 'broadcast.>' to match the 'broadcast.all' subject used in code.

findings.title: Durable consumer name collision in subscribe
findings.explanation: The durable consumer name `channel-${channel}-${currentModelId}` is shared across all instances of the same model ID and channel. If multiple processes or restarts occur, the second consumer will get 'Consumer already exists' error because NATS enforces durable name uniqueness. This breaks reconnection and recovery.
findings.fix: Include a unique instance ID (like testRunId) in the durable name, or use non-durable consumers if message loss on restart is acceptable.

findings.title: Redis xadd stream key does not match NATS subject structure
findings.explanation: When storing broadcast messages, messageId.split(':')[0] yields 'broadcast' for 'broadcast:<id>', so history is stored under 'history:broadcast'. But direct messages use 'direct:<id>' and go to 'history:direct'. This works functionally but creates an inconsistent and non-scalable history key structure that doesn't support per-channel broadcast history.
findings.fix: Align stream key logic with actual channel semantics. For broadcast, use a fixed key like 'history:broadcast', not derived from messageId.

findings.title: Heartbeat handler in modelComms.js overwrites model state without ensuring 'startedAt' is preserved
findings.explanation: The `setModelState` call in the heartbeat handler does not explicitly merge `startedAt` from the existing state. If `existing` has a `startedAt` key, it will be overwritten by the new state object, potentially losing the original start time of the model. This breaks the assumption that `startedAt` is immutable once set.
findings.fix: Change the line to: `await redis.setModelState(modelId, { ...existing, status: 'online', lastHeartbeat: Date.now(), startedAt: existing?.startedAt || null });`

findings.title: Unused `consumerGroup` parameter in natsController.js `subscribe` function
findings.explanation: The `consumerGroup` parameter is optional and defaults to a generated string, but the function does not document or utilize this fallback behavior meaningfully. While it works as intended, it is suboptimal because the parameter could be removed or clarified in its purpose.
findings.fix: Either document the fallback behavior clearly or remove the unused flexibility if it is not needed.

findings.title: Inconsistent `isOnline` calculation in redisController.js `getAllModels` function
findings.explanation: The `isOnline` field is derived from a 60-second threshold, but this logic is not documented or validated across other parts of the system. While it works as expected here, it introduces a potential assumption mismatch if other components use a different definition of 'online'.
findings.fix: Add a comment clarifying this threshold or ensure consistency across components that handle model online/offline states.

findings.title: Test suite in test-comms.js assumes singleton behavior of modelComms.js but bypasses it for models B and C
findings.explanation: The test suite directly uses `nats` and `redis` for models B and C while initializing model A with `modelComms`. This bypasses the singleton pattern assumed in `modelComms`, creating a scenario where the state for model B and C is not fully managed by the API. This can lead to integration issues if `modelComms` expects exclusive control over NATS and Redis state for all models.
findings.fix: Refactor the test to either use `modelComms` for all models or explicitly document and handle the singleton limitation in the testing framework.

findings.title: NATS subscription leak on test cleanup
findings.explanation: The test creates NATS subscriptions but never unsubscribes. This will cause memory leaks and potential duplicate message processing in subsequent test runs or production. The NATS client maintains durable consumers, so these subscriptions persist even after the test completes.
findings.fix: Store the subscription object returned by nats.subscribe() and call sub.unsubscribe() in a cleanup step after each test.

findings.title: Race condition in modelComms initialization
findings.explanation: If multiple models initialize simultaneously, the NATS subscription for direct messages may be created before the directMessageHandler is set, causing messages to be silently dropped. The handler is set via onDirectMessage() which can be called after init().
findings.fix: Move the directMessageHandler assignment before the NATS subscription in init(), or add a null check and queue messages until the handler is set.

findings.title: Redis connection leak in monitor.js
findings.explanation: The monitor CLI mode connects to Redis and NATS but never closes the connections on shutdown. This will cause resource leaks and prevent clean process termination. The shutdown handler only calls stop() which clears the interval but doesn't close Redis/NATS.
findings.fix: Add await nats.close(); await redis.close(); to the shutdown handler in CLI mode.

findings.title: Inconsistent message ID format between NATS and Redis
findings.explanation: The message ID generation in modelComms.js uses a random suffix, but the test-comms.js expects deterministic IDs for verification. While not breaking, this makes testing brittle and could cause issues if message IDs are used for deduplication across systems.
findings.fix: Standardize on either deterministic IDs (e.g., modelId + timestamp + counter) or document the randomness requirement.

findings.title: Missing error handling in modelComms heartbeat
findings.explanation: While errors are caught and logged, repeated heartbeat failures will cause the model to appear offline even though it's still running. This could trigger false alarms in the monitoring system.
findings.fix: Add a retry mechanism or exponential backoff for heartbeat failures, and consider emitting a 'degraded' status after multiple failures.

findings.title: NATS stream subject mismatch in natsController.js
findings.explanation: The CITY_DIRECT stream is configured with subject 'direct.>', but modelComms.js publishes to 'direct.{modelId}' (line 67) and subscribes to 'direct.{modelId}' (line 45). The '>' wildcard only matches at least one token, so 'direct.modelId' won't match 'direct.>'. This breaks direct messaging entirely.
findings.fix: Change the subject to 'direct.*' for the CITY_DIRECT stream to match the exact one-token pattern used in modelComms.js.

findings.title: Redis TTL inconsistency in setMessage
findings.explanation: The Redis message TTL is set to 24 hours, but the NATS stream max_age is set to 24 hours in nanoseconds (line 31 in natsController.js). This creates a temporal inconsistency where messages may disappear from Redis before they expire in NATS, breaking message history retrieval.
findings.fix: Align the TTLs by either setting Redis TTL to 24 hours in seconds (86400) and NATS max_age to 86400 * 1e9, or document the intentional difference.

findings.explanation: The heartbeat merge only preserves existing fields but overwrites any custom state with the hardcoded {status, lastHeartbeat} object. If a model sets custom state fields (e.g., {status: 'online', role: 'coordinator'}), the role field will be lost on the next heartbeat.

allFindings.title: NATS subscription in modelComms uses same durable name across multiple instances
allFindings.explanation: The durable consumer name `consumer-${modelId}` is the same for each model. However, if multiple instances of the same modelId subscribe (e.g., after a restart), they will conflict because NATS JetStream durable consumers must be unique per subscription group. The code in natsController.js uses opts.durable(consumerGroup) and opts.deliverTo(createInbox()) which creates a queue subscription. If two instances use same durable name, they will compete for messages, but the deliverTo creates a unique inbox, causing mismatch and potential message loss.
allFindings.fix: Either make the durable name unique per instance (e.g., include a random suffix) or ensure only one subscriber per modelId exists.

allFindings.fix: Move the directMessageHandler assignment before the NATS subscription in init(), or add a null check and queue messages until the handler is set.
